title: WPSS/612/2023 of MAMTA PANDEY Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 612 of 2023
Mamta Pandey ..............Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ..........Respondents
Present:-
Mr. Harendra Belwal, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Additional Chief Standing Counsel
with Mr. Suyesh Pant, Standing Counsel for the
State/respondents.
JUDGMENT

Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
The petitioner sought compassionate
appointment on the death of her mother on 12.11.2012,
who was working in the Animal Husbandry Department
leaving behind the petitioner and her sister Tanuja
Pandey. The initial application seeking compassionate
appointment given by the petitioner to the respondent
authority was returned on 26.04.2013 by the respondent
no.4, Chief Veterinary Officer, Animal Husbandry
informing that the petitioner may not be entitled for
compassionate appointment because married daughter
does not come under the definition of a family under The
U.P. Recruitment Of Depandants Of Government Servants

2
Dying In Harness Rules, 1974 (for short, "the 1974
Rules").
2. The petitioner moved fresh representations on
16.04.2019 and 03.06.2019. When they did not find
favour, the petitioner did file Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1833
of 2019, Manta Pandey vs. State of Uttarakhand and
others (for short, "the first petition"), which was decided
on 07.12.2021. In fact, it so happened that in between
this Court in Special Appeal No.187 of 2017, Udham
Singh Nagar District Cooperative Bank Ltd. & another vs.
Anjula Singh and others, on 27.03.2019 observed that a
married daughter is to be included under the definition of
a family under Rule 2(c) of the 1974 Rules.
3. In its order dated 07.12.2021, passed in the
first petition the Court observed that the Full Bench
judgment in the case of Anjula Singh (supra) cannot be
made retrospective effect. The petition was dismissed.
Against the judgment and order dated 07.12.2021,
passed in the first petition, the petitioner preferred
Special Appeal, which was allowed on 21.02.2022. The
Court observed:-
"4. Hence, we allow the Special Appeal, set-aside the
judgment passed by the learned Single Judge, and direct the

3
State Authorities i.e. respondent nos.1 to 4 to reconsider the
case of the appellant-petitioner on merit, as per law, and
communicate the same to her within a period of forty-five
days from the date of production of a certified copy of this
judgment before the respondent no.1"
4. It is thereafter, the representation of the
petitioner was rejected on 26.05.2022, on the ground that
the judgment passed by this Court in the case of Anjula
Singh (supra) shall have no retrospective effect. This order
was communication to the petitioner by the respondent
no.3 on 27.05.2022. Both these orders are impugned.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that post judgment in the case of Anjula Singh
(supra), a question arose, as to what would be the effect of
the judgment in the case of Anjula Singh (supra)? And;
whether it would have retrospective effect? It is argued
that the matter was referred to the Full Bench of this
Court in Writ Petition (S/S) No.1214 of 2021, Namrata
Sharma vs. The Director General of Department of
Medical Health and others, which was decided on
17.10.2022 and this Court has held that the ratio laid
down in the case of Anjula Singh (supra) shall be
applicable to all the cases and the cases that may be filed
in future, but it will not open the settled cases in terms
the cases attained finality by the orders of the Court. He

4
would refer in paras 7 and 8 of the judgment in the case
of Namrata Sharma (supra) which are as below:-
"7. Thus, in answering the questions, set forth by
the learned Single Judge, this Court is of the opinion
that since there is no mention in the conclusion given
by the Full Bench of this Court that such law declared
by this Court will be applicable only prospectively not
retrospectively it has to be taken a declaration of law
applicable to all cases retrospectively. However, in this
case we take note of the fact that the petitioner has
already approached this Court twice. Once, before the
pronouncement of the Full Bench judgment in WPSB
No. 391 of 2013, Which has already been decided
against her. Thus, the judgment declaring the law of
the Full Bench will not reopen settled cases. It can be
applied to only case which are pending before this
Court or which will be filed in the future date. By virtue
of the judgment passed by the Full Bench of this Court
referred to above, a right which has already been
denied and the court has not interfered with the same,
then the same cannot be re-agitated in view of the fact
that the law has been restated by the Full Bench in the
later judgment.
8. As far as applicability of time limit provided in
Rule 5, Sub-rule (1) clause (iii) of Rules 1974 that the
application for employment is within five years from the
death of the Government servant, we are of the opinion
that such five years shall be counted in the case of a
married daughter, who has applied for rehabilitation
assistance under the Dying in Harness Rules 1974, as
applicable to the State of Uttarakhand after
amendments in the Rules 2004, 2010 and 2017, shall
be calculated from the date of judgment of Full Bench.
We take this view because of the fact that before the
judgment pronounced by the Full Bench of this Court

5
on 25.03.2019 in SPA No. 187 of 2017, a married
daughter had no opportunity of filing an application for
rehabilitation assistance. Hence, the matter is
answered in the following terms:-
(i) The judgment passed by the Full Bench of this
Court will have a retrospective effect in the sense
that it may be applicable to any case where death
took place after passing of the Rule but before
judgment is pronounced.
(ii) The time period will be calculated from the
date of such judgment as far as dependent
married daughter of an employee dying in
harness applies. In other words, if any person
whose father has died prior to the judgment, she
can make an application for rehabilitation
assistance within five years from the date of
passing of the judgment in SPA No. 187 of 2017."
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that the petitioner's claim to seek compassionate
appointment was not considered in the year 2012 by the
respondents authority and her application was merely
returned on the ground that she does not fall under the
definition of family, as defined under the 1974 Rules. It
has not been challenged in the Court up-till the judgment
passed in the case of Anjula Singh (supra). Therefore, he
would submit that the case of the petitioner has never
been settled by any Court and it is covered by the
judgment passed in the case of Anjula Singh (supra).

6
7. Learned State counsel would admit the
proposition of law. Although, learned State counsel would
submit that the petitioner has another sister Tanuja
Pandey. She is not made a party and there may be
another consideration while deciding an application for
appointment under the provisions of the 1974 Rules. He
would submit that the appointment under the 1974 Rules
may not be claimed as a matter of right and the sole
object of the 1974 Rules is to help the depandants of
Government servants from in their financial crises.
8. Learned State counsel would submit that the
mother of the petitioner died in the year 2012 and since
the petitioner has been able to maintain herself since
2012 for almost 11 years now, it is also a relevant
consideration to establish that the petitioner does not
deserve compassionate appointment.
9. The Court is not called upon to decide the
entitlement of the applicant for appointment, as such
under the 1974 Rules. What is challenged is that the
claim of the petitioner has not been entertained on the
ground that the judgment passed in the case of Anjula
Singh (supra) is not applicable in her case.

7
10. Once the application for appointment under
the 1974 Rules is entertained, perhaps all the factors
which entitles a depandant of Government Servants for
appointment under the 1974 Rules would be examined,
but it has never been done.
11. The limited question, which this Court is
answering in this order is, as to whether the judgment
passed in the case of Anjula Singh (supra) may be
applicable to the petitioner or in other words, whether the
application of the petitioner for seeking appointment
under the 1974 Rules may be entertained in light of the
judgment in the case of Anjula Singh (supra)? The answer
is in affirmative for the following reasons:-
(i) The judgment in the case of Anjula Singh
(supra) was given on 27.03.2019. Till that date,
the petitioner's claim has never been denied by
the respondent authority.
(ii) Till 27.03.2019 the petitioner has never
approached the Court seeking appointment
under the 1974 Rules or challenging any other
order passed by any authority.
(iii) As stated, in the year 2013, the application
which was given by the petitioner initially in

8
the year 2012, seeking appointment under the
1974 Rules, was merely returned. At that stage
also, the claim was not considered on merits.
At that point of time, her application was
returned on a ground that a married daughter
does not fall within the definition of family
under the 1974 Rules.
(iv) After the judgment in the case of Anjula Singh
(supra), when the petitioner made
representation and she did not find response
from the respondents, she filed first writ
petition which was rejected on the ground that
the judgment in the case of Anjula Singh
(supra) may not give any benefit to the
petitioner. But, as stated, in the Special
Appeal, the respondents-authority was directed
to consider the claim of the petitioner. It has
further been denied by the impugned order on
the ground that the petitioner may not get the
benefit of Full Bench judgment passed in the
case of Anjula Singh (supra). This ground for
rejection is bad in view of the judgment given
by this Court in the case of Namrata Sharma
(supra).

9
(v) At the cost of repetition, this
Court reproduces what this Court held in
the case of Namrata Sharma (supra) with
regard to applicability of the judgment
passed in the case of Anjula Singh
(supra). This Court has held, "it can be
applied to only cases, which are
pending before this Court or which will
be filed in the future dates."
12. In view of the judgment given in the case of
Namrata Sharma (supra), the impugned order dated
26.05.2022 and 27.05.2022 are bad in the eyes of law.
They deserve to be set aside. Both these orders are set
aside. The respondent authorities are directed to
entertain the claim of the petitioner within the four
corners of the 1974 Rules on merits.
13. This Court makes it clear that this Court has
not made any observation with regard to the entitlement
of the petitioner for the appointment under the 1974
Rules. What the Court has decided is, her application
need to be considered in view of the judgment given by
this Court in case of Anjula Singh (supra), in accordance
with the 1974 Rules. Accordingly the writ petition
deserves to be allowed.

10
14. With the above observation, the writ petition is
allowed.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 16.06.2023
Sanjay
